answer: Inter-arrival jitter fingerprinting. Each identity must emit its first N transactions with a timing profile matching a reference kernel of human-paced bursts; agents whose gaps are too regular or too synchronized get throttled. The pigment of a sybil cluster is its shared periodicity, detectable without content. Every extra identity therefore costs the attacker fresh randomized scheduling infrastructure and a slower ramp, since bursting is penalized—an opal of patience they must spend per account.
